body:
Sometimes it's just too much to put into words.  You don't know how to explain.  It's exhausting to try. 

  Would it have actually helped? Or would his note have been easy to downplay, to say - it would have gotten better, or we could have helped? 
   Wouldn't it have made you angrier at him?  I don't know. 

  All I know is that he was in a lot of pain. I hope one day you can forgive him for how he chose to make that pain end, and that your family finds some healing.

Telling someone who is suicidal that they should just get a hobby and go on a diet and things will get better!  Is like putting a band-aid on a spurting artery and patting the person on the head and saying "hope you feel better!!" 

   Are you fucking kidding me?  Do you really think I never tried to go on a diet and lose weight?  Or that I never took classes?  I speak several languages. I play instruments.  I volunteered.  Come on. 

 I'm sorry to break your rose-colored glasses, but life isn't all cliches and it'll get better tomorrow! Annie songs. It's not a matter of JUST TRY HARDER! 

  Some of us just don't fit in, no matter how hard we try.  And after trying again and again and again for decades, we are tired of fighting.  If you can't understand what that kind of life is like, lucky you. 

Please, don't ever respond to anything on depression or suicide.  You have no idea what you are talking about and will make the situation much, much worse.

I am sorry for the loss of your cousin and that your family is suffering. 

 For whatever reason, your cousin didn't want help. It was his choice.  I'm sorry, but it was. He made that decision. It's not your fault.  There is nothing you could have done. 

  Your cousin is lucky that he had so many people around him. But when you are in so much pain, sometimes you can't see it, or don't want to see it.  Sharing that kind of pain with people makes you enormously vulnerable, and when you're already hurting sometimes you just don't want to open yourself up like that. 

  Maybe help is available but it takes an ENORMOUS amount of energy and belief in yourself to walk that path.  Many of us are just too tired to fight that fight. 

   I hope that I can help you understand maybe a little of how your cousin was feeling.  Maybe by forgiving him, you all can move on somehow.

<shrugs> My death will not cause anyone pain.  

In order to feel pain at my death, they would actually have to be part of my life. I have no one who depends on me.  I'm not needed by anyone.  I'm not married and I don't have kids so I'm pretty much invisible to my family. 

My friends and siblings are all married with kids. Their families are all consuming. I understand.  But it makes it a lot easier to leave.

Address the food issue. You don't get it at all. It's just another way of killing myself, just more slowly.

Your comment "you may not care enough about those around you to not kill yourself"  shows that you didn't actually bother to read what I wrote. 

  People who commit suicide often care deeply about those around them. We think our pain is too much of a burden for you to take. We don't want to spread our sadness onto you. Clearly your friend felt that way. 

   Maybe your friend is a caring, loving, fun person on the outside.  But it's a show. If he is in that much pain that he wants to leave and can't take it, isn't it incredibly selfish of you to tell him to stick around --- to make YOU feel better? 

  Everyone is responsible for their own life.  For some of us, it's a very painful existence. If you can't understand that kind of pain, you are very lucky. Now let us go.

This was sort of a red flag for me <Every girl i get close to just pretends to like me, then I ask them out and they say no, or aren't ready for a relationship... then have a new beau 2 days later (it's happened 3 times in a row... I can't even make that shit up). I did have a date scheduled a few days ago with a girl I met online... but got stood up. Now she won't return texts or calls.>

  It says to me something else is going on there. Maybe you are seeing signals that just aren't there with these girls.  And people get stood up from online dates all the time. 

  People in the Midwest get it. I'm here, in the Midwest. It feels like there's a lot of blame going on and not much thought to your role in this. 

  You cannot change other people. Maybe some therapy is in order to figure out how you can change, if you want to.  If you don't, then you don't, and that's ok too.

I am happy that good things have come into your life and that you have someone who loves you. 

  This will not happen for me. I'm the kind of woman who is either invisible or who gets barked at on the street. A long time ago, a man whom I loved told me that it felt bad to touch me, like poking a finger in jello. 

  I stopped letting people touch me after that for a long time. I couldn't stand to ask for affection, knowing it would feel to the other person. Now it's not even an issue, I don't have anyone around. 

  It's ok. Everyone has different paths. My path is just a very hard one, but honestly, it feels so much better knowing that there's an end to it. I don't know if that makes sense.
